seo.title: Healthcare website design and development
seo.description: Accessible, multi-location healthcare websites with privacy-first appointment booking, provider directories and content clinic staff update themselves.

answerBlock: A healthcare website has to help a patient find the right clinic and clinician and book or request an appointment, accessibly and on any device, without exposing health information. Calwebtech builds multi-location healthcare websites with provider directories, location-aware booking and forms designed around patient privacy. Clinic staff update opening hours, providers and services themselves, with no developer involved.

hero.intro: Patients arrive anxious, often on a phone and sometimes with assistive technology. We design every path around finding the right location and booking a visit, and we keep tracking tools away from anything a patient types.
highlights: Location and provider search that works on a phone
Appointment booking connected to your scheduling system
Built and tested to WCAG 2.2 AA
Clinic staff publish their own updates

painPoints.heading: Why do healthcare websites frustrate patients and staff?
painPoints.intro: Most of the problems come from websites that grew one clinic at a time.

items.title: One website per clinic
items.body: Acquisitions and new locations each brought their own site, so opening hours, providers and services are maintained in several places and are wrong in at least one.

items.title: Booking means a phone call
items.body: Patients who want to book in the evening find a phone number, and front desk staff spend the next morning returning calls an online request could have handled.

items.title: Accessibility as an afterthought
items.body: Low contrast, unlabelled forms and PDFs that screen readers cannot read shut out patients who rely on assistive technology, and expose the organisation to complaints.

items.title: Waiting days for a website change
items.body: A new provider, a changed phone number or a seasonal clinic depends on an agency ticket, so the website is always a few changes behind the practice.

services.heading: Which services does a healthcare organisation need from a web partner?
services.intro: Healthcare projects usually consolidate several sites into one platform before adding booking.

items.title: WordPress development
items.body: A WordPress platform for multi-location groups, with locations, providers and services as structured content your staff already know how to edit.

items.title: Custom website development
items.body: Patient-first design for finding care: service and condition pages, location search and provider profiles written in plain language.

items.title: Web application development
items.body: Appointment request and booking flows, intake forms and referral portals connected to your scheduling system.

items.title: Website redesign
items.body: Merging several clinic websites into one without losing the local search visibility each location has earned.

items.title: Website care plans
items.body: Security patching, uptime monitoring, backups with a tested restore and accessibility checks on new content, month to month.

compliance.heading: What privacy and accessibility rules does a healthcare website have to meet?
compliance.intro: Patient privacy is often lost on the website, through a form or a tracking script nobody reviewed. We design these rules in from the first template and review the set-up with your compliance lead.

notes.title: Health information in forms
notes.body: Appointment and intake forms collect only what is needed, travel over encrypted connections and are stored with access controls. Any third-party tool that handles patient information needs a HIPAA business associate agreement before it goes live.

notes.title: Tracking technologies
notes.body: Analytics and advertising pixels can disclose health information to third parties, so we keep them off appointment, patient and condition pages and load analytics only after consent.

notes.title: Accessibility
notes.body: We build to WCAG 2.2 AA and test with keyboards and screen readers. Federal rules for providers that receive HHS funding point to WCAG 2.1 AA, which a 2.2 AA build covers.

notes.title: Clinical content review
notes.body: Condition and treatment pages carry a named clinical reviewer and a review date, managed in the dashboard, so medical content stays current and accountable.

integrations.heading: Which systems does a healthcare website usually connect to?
integrations.intro: Patient records stay in the clinical systems. The website connects to them only where the vendor offers a supported interface.

items.name: Scheduling and practice management
items.body: athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, NextGen and similar systems, through their scheduling APIs or approved booking widgets.

items.name: Patient portals
items.body: Clear links into the portal your EHR provides, such as Epic MyChart, rather than a second login on the website.

items.name: Telehealth
items.body: Links to your telehealth platform from booking confirmations and provider profiles.

items.name: Listings and reviews
items.body: Location details kept consistent with Google Business Profile and directory listings for every clinic.

items.name: HIPAA-eligible forms
items.body: Form and storage services that sign a business associate agreement, for intake that has to collect health information.

items.name: Referral intake
items.body: Referrals routed to the right clinic team, with patient information kept out of marketing systems.

faq.heading: What do healthcare teams ask before a new website?
faq.intro: The questions practice managers, marketing leads and compliance officers raise first.

items.question: Can patients book appointments directly on the website?
items.answer: Yes, where your scheduling system allows it. Many practice management systems offer booking APIs or approved widgets; where yours does not, we build an appointment request flow that routes to the right location and confirms by email. We confirm which applies in discovery.

items.question: Is the website HIPAA compliant?
items.answer: HIPAA governs how protected health information is handled, not a website on its own. We keep health information out of general forms and tracking, use services that sign a business associate agreement wherever patient information is collected, and document the set-up so your compliance lead can review it.

items.question: Can several clinic locations share one website?
items.answer: Yes, and it is usually the right call. Each location gets its own page with hours, providers, services and directions for local search, while content that applies everywhere is written once.

items.question: How do you make a healthcare website accessible?
items.answer: We build to WCAG 2.2 AA as the working standard: sufficient contrast, labelled form fields with clear errors, full keyboard operation and a correct heading order. We test with keyboards and screen readers before launch, and care plans include checks on new content.

items.question: Can our staff update provider profiles and opening hours themselves?
items.answer: Yes. Providers, locations, services and hours are content types with simple editors and roles, so a clinic manager can update their own location without touching the rest of the site and without a deployment.

items.question: How much does a healthcare website cost?
items.answer: A single-location website with custom design and appointment requests usually sits in our focused build range of $12k to $25k. Multi-location platforms with provider directories, booking integration and site consolidation are platform builds, usually $25k to $60k.
